span.backdrop: --gradient-dark #1A1F36 -> #2D3348, plus brand circles at 0.10 and 0.08 opacity
span.method: worst glyph stop against the worst backdrop point. Conservative: the glyphs are a gradient, so part of the word clears the threshold even where the first stop does not, and WCAG has no rule for 'some of the letters pass'.
span.superseded_by: the original excuse, '4.47:1 at the worst pair of stops, 9.28:1 at the best' (3ac024e4), which is #FF6B5B on #2D3348 and #FFB199 on #1A1F36 — the template default, not any brand.
span.verdict: FAILS. violet on every reading; coastal and demo_title on all but the darkest backdrop point with no tint; luxury_estates only with the tint. D-206.
span.why_unmeasurable: harbor_report.jinja2:52 paints .cover-title span with --gradient-coral clipped to the glyphs via -webkit-text-fill-color:transparent, which is the property the measurer uses to blank text. Blanking changes nothing, so the sampled backdrop is the element's own gradient and the reported foreground is not what the reader sees.
